The maximum possible sum is the total variation of \(f\) on \([1,4]\).

Since \(f\) decreases on \([1,2]\) and increases on \([2,4]\):

\[
|f(1)-f(2)| + |f(2)-f(4)|
= |-2 - (-3)| + |-3 - 1|
= 1 + 4 = 5.
\]

This is achieved by choosing \(x_1=1,\ x_2=2,\ x_3=4\). Thus the smallest such \(M\) is

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
